You cannot transitiely pull in annotation processors as far as I know. So if you dont have it in your POM it won't work.
There are obviously cases you can create where you have lombok without having it explitily in your main build
for example
```kotlin
plugins {
  id(`a-plugin-that-adds-lombok-as-ap`)
}
```
or a parent POM in maven.
I think its an improvement it will work in +90% of cases. Of course the most reliable way would be to let gradle/maven dump their annotationProcessor paths & classpaths and then read that but thats too much complexity/time/cpu for this issue imo.

These tests create instances via `Instance.provide` for each tmp directory but never dispose them. Since `Instance` caches contexts globally and `tmpdir()` cleanup doesn’t dispose `Instance`, this can leak resources/state and make the suite flaky over time. Consider adding an `afterEach` cleanup (e.g., `Instance.disposeAll()`) or disposing inside the tmp scope.

**Style: Use `Filesystem.exists()` or `pathExists()` helper instead of `Bun.file().exists()`**

**Style: Use `Filesystem.writeStream()` pattern instead of `Bun.file().write()`**

Other LSP servers use `if (response.body) await Filesystem.writeStream(path, response.body)` for downloading (see ElixirLS at line 559, Zls at line 666, etc.). This handles the response body properly.

**Style: Use `Process.spawn()` instead of `Bun.spawn()`**

Other LSP servers use `Process.spawn()` for running installation commands (see Gopls at line 361, Rubocop at line 400, CSharp at line 718, etc.).

**Style: Prefer shorter variable name**

Per style guide, prefer single-word names where clear. Consider `dir` instead of `installDir` since context makes the intent clear.

The initialization logic clears the variant with `local.model.variant.set(undefined)` when the last user message has no variant or when its variant matches the agent-configured default. In `LocalContext`, `variant.set(undefined)` is persisted as the explicit "default" sentinel (see `setModelStore("variant", key, value ?? "default")`), which will be interpreted as an explicit user override and will *disable* the agent’s configured variant rather than “unsetting” the override. Introduce a real “unset”/delete path for the stored selection (so agent defaults can apply), and only persist the "default" sentinel when the user explicitly chooses Default.

This block recomputes the configured agent variant by re-looking-up the agent info and provider model metadata. Since `LocalContext` now has `local.model.variant.configured()`, consider using that directly (after setting agent/model) to avoid duplicating the match/variant-availability logic in multiple places and risking future divergence.

The request queue is released as soon as `fetchFn(...)` resolves, but `fetch()` resolves when response headers arrive. For streaming/SSE model calls (used via `streamText`), that means the lock is released while the model is still generating tokens, so subsequent requests can overlap and still overload local inference servers. Consider holding the lock until the response body stream is fully consumed/closed (e.g., wrap/pipe the Response body and only resolve the queue on stream completion/cancel), or move serialization to the higher-level LLM call site so it covers the full request lifecycle.

`globalRequestQueue` serializes *all* provider HTTP calls across the entire process (including cloud providers). This can significantly reduce throughput for remote backends and also makes one slow/hung request block every other agent/session. If the intent is to protect local backends, consider scoping the queue to local baseURLs (e.g., localhost/127.0.0.1) or maintaining a queue per provider/baseURL so unrelated providers don’t contend.

Creating 2,000 files via `Promise.all(ids.map(...Filesystem.write...))` can be slow/flaky on CI (especially Windows) due to high parallel I/O and potential EMFILE. Consider batching with bounded concurrency and/or lowering the count while keeping the total pathspec length large enough to reproduce the ENAMETOOLONG scenario.

This second `Promise.all` rewrites the same 2,000 files in parallel, compounding the I/O load for the test suite. Consider reusing the initial contents via fewer modifications, batching writes, or lowering the file count to minimize runtime while still exceeding command-line length limits.

Large files (> limit) are excluded from staging via `stage(allow.filter(!large.has(...)))`, but they can still remain tracked in the snapshot index from earlier runs. In that case `write-tree` will continue to capture the *previous* blob for that path (silently producing a snapshot that doesn’t match the current worktree), and `restore` may overwrite the user’s current large file with stale contents. Consider explicitly removing newly-large paths from the snapshot index (similar to the gitignored handling) so future snapshots/restore stop touching them, or otherwise make the behavior explicit (e.g., log + keep staged updates for already-tracked large files).

This change switches to `--stdin` / `--pathspec-from-file=-` to avoid command-line length limits (ENAMETOOLONG). There isn’t an obvious regression test exercising a very large candidate set (thousands of paths) to ensure snapshotting still works on platforms with tight argv limits (notably Windows). Consider adding an integration test that creates many modified/untracked files and verifies `track()`/`patch()` succeed and include the expected subset, so this fix stays covered.

`aliases["@/"]` is computed as `path.join(srcDir, "/")`, which resolves to the filesystem root (or drive root) rather than `srcDir`. That will cause most `@/...` imports to be treated as non-local / unresolvable, preventing Rollup from traversing and tree-shaking internal modules. Use `srcDir` (optionally with a trailing separator) instead of joining with `"/"`.

Setting `treeshake.moduleSideEffects = false` tells Rollup that *no* modules have side effects, which can drop required bare imports. This repo has bare side-effect imports like `import "opentui-spinner/solid"` (e.g. `src/cli/cmd/tui/component/spinner.tsx`), which are needed for runtime registration; Rollup may remove them and break the CLI. Consider removing this override, or make `moduleSideEffects` a function that preserves side effects for externals / specific packages while still enabling the desired barrel tree-shaking.

`transform()` constructs a new `Bun.Transpiler` for every file, which can add noticeable overhead given the number of modules Rollup will parse. Cache a single transpiler per loader (`ts`/`tsx`) (or reuse one transpiler instance) to reduce the pre-pass runtime.

`MessageV2.usage()` never verifies that the session exists. For an unknown `sessionID`, both queries return no rows and the function returns `{ last: undefined, totalCost: 0 }`, which makes `GET /session/:sessionID/usage` respond 200 instead of 404 (and contradicts the route's documented `...errors(400, 404)` behavior). Consider mirroring `MessageV2.page()`'s pattern: when no matching messages are found, check `SessionTable` for the session id and throw `NotFoundError` if missing; otherwise return the empty snapshot for an existing session with no assistant messages.

The comment says this polling is for the desktop app, but the implementation will run anywhere this page is used (including web) whenever the project is git. Consider gating the interval using the Platform context (e.g., `usePlatform().platform === "desktop"`) and/or only polling when the changes/review panel is visible to avoid unnecessary background invalidations/refetches on web.

This interval is only created inside `onMount()` and only if `sync.project?.vcs === "git"` at mount time. `sync.project` can be undefined initially (child store starts with `project: ""` and is set during bootstrap), so the fallback polling may never start even once the project is resolved. Consider using a reactive `createEffect` that starts/stops the interval when `sync.project?.vcs` becomes available/changes, instead of checking only at mount.

Why this is herer:
When the session loop processes tool calls, each round-trip creates a new assistant message. Intermediate messages get finish === "tool-calls" or "other", so they don't show the footer bar. Their tool parts are also hidden by default (when showDetails is off and the tool completed successfully). If such a message has no text or reasoning either, it renders as an empty fragment -- but it still occupies a slot in the parent <For> loop, producing visible blank space in the TUI.

The visible() memo checks whether the message would actually produce any rendered output (a visible text/tool/reasoning part, a footer, or an error box). If nothing would render, the entire <Show when={visible()}> hides the message, eliminating the blank space. It's reactive to showDetails() and showThinking(), so toggling those settings correctly reveals previously hidden messages.
